dewalt-20v-max-drill-impact-combo:
Short answer

Buy the DCK240C2 if you want your first cordless drill and impact driver in one box, from a brand with service centers everywhere, with two batteries, a charger and a bag included. Skip it if you already own DEWALT 20V MAX batteries (buy the bare tools instead) or if you drill big holes in hardwood or steel every day (a bigger, higher-end kit with larger batteries fits that better). Every spec below is from DEWALT's DCK240C2 page or DEWALT's DCD771 manual, checked Nov 10, 2026. No prices here.

What is in the box (DEWALT's list)

  • (1) DCD771 20V MAX 1/2 inch drill/driver
  • (1) DCF885 20V MAX 1/4 inch impact driver
  • (2) 20V MAX 1.3Ah lithium ion battery packs
  • (1) 20V MAX charger
  • (1) contractor bag

No drill bits or driver bits are listed in the kit, so plan on a bit set too.

Use notes: which tool for which job

  • Drill/driver for holes and small screws. Use gear 1 (slide the shifter toward the chuck) for more torque and big bits, gear 2 for speed with small bits. The numbered clutch collar stops the screw from sinking too deep: start low and turn it up.
  • Impact driver for long screws and lag bolts. Deck screws, cabinet screws and lag bolts are its job. It only takes 1/4 inch hex shank bits, so use impact rated bits.
  • Stop the motor before you shift gears on the drill. DEWALT's manual says to let it stop first.
  • 1.3Ah packs are small and light. That keeps the tools easy to hold overhead, but for a long job keep one pack on the charger while you use the other.
  • Store batteries indoors. Heat and freezing cold are hard on lithium ion packs.

Who should buy it

  • Homeowners and renters starting a tool collection who want a drill and an impact driver that share batteries.
  • Handymen and side gig workers who want a light pair for furniture assembly, shelves, TV mounts and fence or deck repairs.
  • Anyone who wants a big brand with easy to find batteries and service.

Who should skip it

  • You already own DEWALT 20V MAX batteries. Buying the bare tools (tool only) usually makes more sense than paying for two more packs and a charger.
  • You drill large holes in hardwood, masonry or steel all day. The 1.3Ah packs and this compact pair are made for lighter work. A hammer drill or a kit with larger packs fits better.
  • You need lug nut power. A 1/4 inch impact driver is not an impact wrench. For tires and trucks, see the EWORK 3/4 inch impact wrench.

What to check before you buy

  • Make sure the listing says DCK240C2 and shows both tools, 2 batteries, the charger and the bag.
  • Plan on a drill bit set and a pack of impact rated driver bits. The DEWALT 14-Piece Drill Bit Set is a cheap add-on.
  • Register the tools with DEWALT after you buy so the warranty paperwork is easy later.

ework-3-4-cordless-impact-wrench:
Who it is for

People who change their own tires, work on trucks or trailers, or fight stuck lug nuts. It is a high-torque, brushless 3/4 inch impact rated in the 1500 ft-lbs class.

How to get the most out of it

  • Use impact-rated sockets, not regular chrome ones.
  • Use it to break lug nuts loose, then finish tightening with a torque wrench to your vehicle's spec.
  • Wear eye protection and keep hands clear of the socket.
  • Charge the battery fully before a big job.

What to check before you buy

  • Make sure 3/4 inch drive matches your sockets, since most home sets are 1/2 inch.
  • It is a lesser-known brand than DEWALT or Milwaukee, so read recent reviews and check the return policy.
  • Torque numbers are the maker's claims, so compare them with real reviews.

Anyone who just bought a drill, or whose old bits are dull, chipped or missing sizes. It is a basic set for wood, metal and plastic around the house.
